notes:
Copilot is a NATIVE self-prompting loop, not an externally-driven one: `/autopilot on` puts the session in autopilot mode and, on every session.idle, tryAutopilotContinuation dispatches its own next prompt (app.js:2398) until the model calls task_complete or --max-autopilot-continues (default 5) is hit. The driver therefore sends EXACTLY ONE prompt for the whole run, and iter2_start is the load-bearing phase: a ready→working transition on the same session with no driver input between it and iter1_end can only have come from copilot re-prompting itself. Each continuation is emitted as a real user.message (the system.notification branch of the shared prompt path needs a notificationKind, which the autopilot send does not supply — app.js:2421), carrying source:"system", agentMode:"autopilot" and EMPTY content; parser.go maps it to EventType user_message → working, and the explicit assistant.turn_end marker settles each iteration → ready. The spec's strict 'stays continuously working' bullet is relaxed exactly as the claudecode sibling relaxed it — continuations fire AFTER turn_end, so the session flickers ready↔working per iteration — and what is asserted instead is the per-iteration arc, the unprompted second iteration, and the no-waiting invariant (--allow-all pre-approves every tool, so permission.requested is structurally unreachable). PRESESSION SHAPE: copilot creates session-state/<id>/ at launch holding only workspace.yaml and writes events.jsonl only on the first prompt, so processlifecycle mints a proc-<PID> row first and the real session arrives under a DIFFERENT id — birth is two phases and every later phase anchors to the real session, templated from the copilot basic-turn sibling. Each iterN_end anchors to its own iterN_start (not to session_birth) so the matcher picks the post-iteration ready rather than the birth ready. OBSERVATIONS: cost and tokens are both live from assistant.message.outputTokens through the shared capacity price map; model is NOT pinned because --model accepts only "auto" on this account and session.auto_mode_resolved picks between gpt-5-mini and claude-haiku-4.5 per turn. PROVISIONAL: daemon=full rests on the continuation being emitted as user.message, which is code-evidenced but not yet recording-evidenced — if the recording shows iter2_start missing, the session sat in ready for the entire autonomous run and this cell is daemon=bug.

RE-RECORDED 2026-08-05 (CLI 1.0.78) — THREE CHANGES, ONE OF WHICH WEAKENS THIS CELL. (1) BIRTH RE-ANCHORED: the real session is born directly into `working` (commit 3cde4f8d), so session_birth and loop_start are ONE phase. (2) COPILOT_AVAILABLE_TOOLS: the cost-saving `--available-tools=bash` restriction aborts autopilot after ONE iteration — session.error{errorType:query, "Required tool 'task_complete' is not available"} — because autopilot closes the objective by calling task_complete. Recorded with bash,task_complete. (3) THE AUTONOMY ASSERTION NO LONGER RIDES ON A STATE TRANSITION, and this is the honest part. The pre-record spec's load-bearing phases were iter1_end (ready) and iter2_start (working) — a ready→working bounce with no driver input, which only copilot's own continuation could produce. Whether that bounce EXISTS is debounce-timing-dependent, not a property of the adapter: in the 2026-08-05 09:42 run the gaps from assistant.turn_end to the next autopilot user.message were 2.4s (> the 2s debounce window) and the daemon emitted discrete ready→working cycles; in the promoted 09:49 run the same recipe produced 0.9s gaps, every continuation coalesced, and the session held ONE continuous 64s `working` span across all three iterations. Both are correct daemon behaviour and neither is reproducible on demand, so asserting either shape would make this cell flaky. The phases below therefore assert only what is stable — one prompt in, a long unbroken working span, a settle to ready, and never waiting — and the autonomy itself is evidenced in the TRANSCRIPT, which is deterministic: the driver sends exactly ONE prompt (07:49:13.684) and events.jsonl then carries THREE MORE user.message records with agentMode:"autopilot" and empty content (07:49:23.465, 07:49:31.392 — plus the initiating one), three bash tool.execution_start records, and a session.task_complete at 07:50:17.880 that ends the loop on the model's own call rather than on the --max-autopilot-continues cap. A non-autonomous session cannot produce those records. ALSO NOTE the recipe now pins the agent's final message to the literal word 'done': the 09:42 run's own completion prose ended '...to create loop3.txt and verify it.', which matches curated imperative pattern D in core/domain/session/waiting_cue.go and routed the settled session to waiting. That is the shared heuristic working as designed (#381 documents the recall-over-precision tradeoff) and NOT a copilot gap — the tailer keeps lastPendingWaitingCue in lockstep with the last NON-EMPTY assistant text (applyAssistantTextAndMarkers), so claudecode and codex carry a stale cue across a text-free tool-call message identically.

text: proc-<PID> pre-session appears in ready shortly after launch (the copilot process exists while the session dir still holds only workspace.yaml)

Spec bullet 1 — 'ready → working at loop start'. The single driver prompt sets the objective while the session is already in autopilot mode, and the real <session-id> session is born DIRECTLY into working because events.jsonl already holds the open turn. It then STAYS working for at least 30s: the driver sends nothing further for the rest of the run, so every second of that span is autonomous work. Corroborating, not conclusive, at the event layer — a single slow turn could also run 30s; the transcript records named in the meta notes are the deterministic autonomy evidence.
copilot PID bound to the real session (matched by cwd from session.start.data.context.cwd)

Spec bullet 6 — 'after the goal is reached: working → ready'. The loop ends on its own (the model calls task_complete, which also flips the mode back to interactive) and the session settles to ready. Across the whole autonomous run the session never entered waiting: the driver launches with --allow-all, so no permission.requested is written, and the recipe pins the final message to a word that carries no prose waiting-cue.
